chunks: And He who sent down from the sky water in due measure, then quickened thereby a dead land -- thus shall you be brought forth.

key_terms.تُخْرَجُونَ: you will be brought forth / resurrected
key_terms.فَأَنْشَرْنَا: then We revived / brought to life

ai.seo_question: How does the Quran use the example of rain to explain resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the phrase 'by measure' (bi-qadar) is often interpreted to signify divine precision in the distribution of rain, serving as a tangible sign of God's ability to precisely orchestrate the resurrection of the dead. This analogy underscores the continuity between natural life cycles and the metaphysical reality of the Hereafter, a core tenet in Shia theological discussions on bodily resurrection. The verse thus bridges the physical and spiritual realms, affirming that the same Creator who sustains the earth is fully capable of raising humanity for judgment.
